brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: piano keyboard mapped to color wheel makes the chord/harmony idea immediately legible and playful
Color wheel rendering is luscious — radial gradient, soft inner glow, and triadic guide lines give a real instrument-panel feel
Right-side properties panel is restrained and information-dense without crowding the hero canvas
dominant_weaknesses: Only one selection dot is shown on the wheel despite 'Major Triad' being active — the chord visualization fails the core promise
Piano keys are tiny, floating, and disconnected from the wheel; the musical-instrument metaphor reads as decoration not interaction
Top-right segmented control duplicates the left preset list (Major/Minor/Triadic/Complement), creating redundant IA and ambiguous state
fix_priorities: Render all harmony points on the wheel simultaneously with connecting geometry so chords visibly 'lock'
Resolve preset duplication — merge top tabs and left list, or differentiate their roles clearly
Scale up and integrate the keyboard with the wheel (e.g., keys as radial segments) to fuse the two metaphors
Tighten typography hierarchy: HEX/RGB/HSL/HSV labels need stronger weight contrast against values
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral pull from the gradient wheel outpaces a thin behavioral layer (chord locking is implied, not shown), leaving reflective satisfaction promised but undelivered.
rationale.intent_fit: Concept aligns with the brief but execution shows a single note rather than a played chord, so the 'harmonies lock like chords' promise is only half-realized.
